author: Spongiform
text:
Hello Ifmyante, harshrthakkar,

I hope you don't mind me dropping in on this.

Harsh, perhaps try to think about who is doing what to whom, rather than
 what the patterns are - if you understand the mechanism behind the
movement of price you'll realise that the patterns themselves aren't as
important as what they convey. ITs need liquidity to enter and exit the
market, and they have the wealth to 'send signals' that manipulate
beliefs in retail traders and herd them into areas where they
effectively trade against the ITs... . Yes patterns do repeat and can be
 used as short-hand, and brains are great at spotting patterns, and ITs
know this, and that's why patterns repeat... .

(And just to misquote Mark Twain, "Patterns do not repeat themselves, but they sure do rhyme.".)

Here's my attempt at If's quiz, I'm not saying my observations are
correct (and they may even be completely wrong), but they show how I try
 to think when I'm looking at a chart. It is much much easier to give
reasons why price should have turned at an area when you already know
that it did, it's not so easy on the hard right edge (at least not for
me!), and we don't know what was going on before we see these patterns
(they may be reactions to Supply and Demand areas).

 Warning: Spoiler!

 [ Click to expand ]

 [ Click to hide ]

The notes are a bit jumbled but read them in numerical order:

Caveat lector!

(And if I'm truly wide of the mark, help wouldn't be turned away )

Regards.

Spongy.
